properties.natural_language: The ecrecover precompile input parameter v must be exactly 27 or 28; any other value must cause an empty return without revert.
The ecrecover precompile input parameter r must satisfy 0 < r < SECP256K1N; values outside this range must cause an empty return.
The ecrecover precompile input parameter s must satisfy 0 < s < SECP256K1N; values outside this range must cause an empty return.
After successful ecrecover execution with valid v, r, s parameters, the output must be a 32-byte value containing the recovered Ethereum address left-padded with 12 zero bytes.
The ecrecover precompile must never revert; on any invalid input or recovery failure, it must return empty output (zero bytes) rather than throwing an exception.
The ecrecover precompile must always consume exactly 3000 gas (GAS_ECRECOVER) regardless of whether the recovery succeeds or fails.
If the calling context has less than 3000 gas available, the ecrecover precompile must fail with an out-of-gas error before any computation.
Input shorter than 128 bytes must be right-padded with zeros before parsing v, r, s parameters.
The ecrecover precompile must accept both low-s and high-s signatures without rejecting either, maintaining backward compatibility.
The ECDSA signature recovery must rely on the computational infeasibility of forging secp256k1 signatures without knowledge of the private key.
The secp256k1_recover implementation must be constant-time to prevent timing side-channel attacks that could leak private key information.
All three validation checks (v range, r range, s range) must pass sequentially before key recovery is attempted.
A validator deposit must be exactly 32 ETH with valid pubkey and withdrawal credentials before entering the activation queue.
The number of validator activations per epoch must never exceed MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT (8), regardless of the total validator set size.
After activation churn limit computation, the result must equal min(get_validator_churn_limit(state), MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT).
After successful validator activation, the validator must transition to active status and be eligible to attest and propose.
Validators that exceed the epoch activation limit must be deferred to the next epoch in FIFO order, preserving queue ordering.
Post-EIP-7514, validator set growth must be linear (bounded by constant per-epoch cap) rather than exponential (scaling with validator set size).
The asymmetry between bounded entry and unbounded exit queues must not cause validator set instability that threatens finality.
An attacker must not be able to exploit asymmetric entry/exit to manipulate validator set composition through coordinated exits and re-entries.
MAX_PER_EPOCH_ACTIVATION_CHURN_LIMIT is a protocol constant that can only be modified via hard fork consensus.
The EIP-7514 churn limit remains in effect until explicitly superseded by another EIP; there is no automatic expiry.
The EVM call depth must never exceed EVM_RECURSION_LIMIT (12288); any nested call at or beyond this depth must fail and return 0.
After a nested call within the recursion limit, the call depth must be incremented by exactly one and execution proceeds normally.
The Python execution environment must have its recursion limit set high enough (>= 12288) to support the EVM_RECURSION_LIMIT.
Both EVM_RECURSION_LIMIT (12288) and EIP-150 gas-based call depth limit (1024) apply simultaneously; the effective limit is the minimum of both.
The package version string must accurately reflect the specification version implemented for client interoperability.
A block received from a peer node must have its RLP-encoded size validated against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) before any expensive processing.
After block size validation, a block with RLP-encoded size <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE must be accepted for further validation.
After block size validation, a block with RLP-encoded size > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE must be rejected and marked invalid.
A finalized block ready for propagation must have its total RLP-encoded size within MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
The 2 MiB safety margin between MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) and the CL limit (~10 MiB) must be maintained to prevent consensus layer constraint violations.
An oversized block from a malicious peer must be rejected via early size check before signature verification or state transition processing.
During block construction, the validator must not add a transaction that would cause the block to exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.
A peer's etha handshake must be validated for networkId, genesis hash, and forkId compatibility before establishing the protocol connection.
After successful handshake validation, the etha protocol connection must be established and ready for data exchange.
A node's block bitmask commitment must accurately reflect the historical data it actually retains; false advertisement constitutes a protocol violation.
Block data falling within a node's bitmask-committed spans must be retained; block data outside committed spans may be pruned.
After identifying peers with matching bitmasks and sending data requests, the node must receive the requested block bodies or receipts, or detect data unavailability.
Nodes with all-zero bitmask contribute no historical data availability but may still consume data from the network.
ENR-based data availability discovery must always be verified through the etha handshake before relying on advertised bitmask claims.
Protocol failures during etha communication must result in connection termination; implementations must handle peer disconnection gracefully.
An attacker must not be able to control enough of the network to make specific historical data spans permanently unavailable.
At transaction execution start, the accessed_addresses set must be initialized with the sender address, recipient address, and all precompile addresses.
After a cold address access, the address must be added to accessed_addresses, making all subsequent accesses to it warm within the same transaction.
Cold address access must be charged 2600 gas, and warm address access must be charged 100 gas; the differential must always be 2500 gas.
Cold SLOAD access must be charged 2100 gas; the SLOAD warm access cost must be 100 gas; SSTORE_RESET_GAS must be 2900.
After a cold storage key access during SSTORE, the (address, storage_key) pair must be added to accessed_storage_keys.
When a call context reverts, all access set modifications made within that scope must be reverted, restoring access sets to the pre-call state.
When a call context succeeds, all access set modifications made within that scope must persist in the parent context.
Contracts making sub-calls with fixed gas limits (e.g., 2300 gas stipend) may fail on cold access due to increased gas costs; pre-warming via earlier access or access lists mitigates this.
After pre-warming an address or storage key, a subsequent sub-call to the same address must succeed with warm access cost (100 gas).
When executing within a contract, the contract's own address must already be in accessed_addresses (warm) due to call setup.
CREATE/CREATE2 must add the newly created contract address to accessed_addresses as part of the creation operation.
Precompile addresses (0x01-0x09 and any chain-specific additions) must be included in the initial accessed_addresses set at transaction start.
The PUSH0 opcode (0x5f) must push exactly the value 0 onto the EVM stack and consume exactly 2 gas (Gbase).
Before PUSH0 execution, the stack size must be less than 1024; otherwise a stack overflow must occur.
After PUSH0 executes successfully, the program counter must advance by exactly 1 (no immediate data bytes).
PUSH0 saves 1 gas and 1 byte compared to PUSH1 0x00, providing consistent gas and bytecode size improvements.
Before EIP-3855 activation, opcode 0x5f must be treated as an invalid opcode causing execution failure; after activation it must execute as PUSH0.
A PUSH0-triggered stack overflow must consume all remaining gas, revert all state changes in the call frame, and return failure.
No existing deployed contract must have its behavior changed by the PUSH0 introduction; 0x5f in data positions must not be reinterpreted as code.
Keccak256 hash computation must be deterministic: the same input bytes must always produce the same 32-byte Hash32 output across all client implementations.
Keccak512 hash computation must be deterministic: the same input bytes must always produce the same 64-byte Hash64 output.
Attackers must not be able to find Keccak256 or Keccak512 collisions in practical time; the security of state roots, transaction hashes, and address derivation depends on collision resistance.
Hash functions must accept any valid bytes/bytearray input without length limits; the underlying Keccak sponge construction handles arbitrary-length inputs.
After hash comparison, matching hashes must confirm data integrity; mismatching hashes must indicate data corruption or tampering.
The underlying Keccak cryptographic primitive implementation must be correct and secure; a compromised hash function would enable collision attacks across all Ethereum operations.
Hash functions are pure computations that must not raise exceptions for valid byte inputs; invalid input types raise standard type errors.
A transaction's gasLimit must be validated against the cap of 16,777,216 (2^24) at both mempool acceptance and block validation stages.
After gas limit validation, transactions with gasLimit <= 16,777,216 must be accepted into the mempool.
After gas limit validation, transactions with gasLimit > 16,777,216 must be rejected and not added to the mempool.
A block received from a peer must have every contained transaction's gasLimit validated against the 16,777,216 cap; any violation invalidates the entire block.
A block containing any transaction with gasLimit > 16,777,216 must be rejected entirely.
The gas cap validation is based solely on the declared gasLimit field, not actual gas usage; a transaction with gasLimit > 16,777,216 is invalid even if execution would use less gas.
A block's total gas may exceed 16,777,216 by including multiple transactions each individually under the cap; the per-transaction cap is independent of the block gas limit.
The gas cap enforcement must bound block validation time to predictable limits, preventing DoS attacks via resource-exhausting transactions.
All legitimate use cases must be accomplishable within the 16,777,216 gas limit or restructured (via CREATE2 factory, proxy patterns, or split deployments) to fit.
A block header submitted for PoW verification must contain a valid header_hash and nonce before the hashimoto algorithm proceeds.
After computing the seed hash via keccak512(header_hash || reversed_nonce), the result must be a 64-byte value used to initialize the mix array.
The hashimoto verification loop must execute exactly 64 iterations, each accessing 2 dataset rows, for a total of 128 dataset accesses.
After all 64 iterations, the mix must be compressed into a 32-byte mix digest via FNV-combining 4-element groups.
The final PoW hash must be computed as keccak256(seed_hash || mix_digest); if this hash is <= the target difficulty, the block passes PoW verification.
Epoch transitions must occur predictably every 30,000 blocks, triggering regeneration of the epoch seed, cache, and dataset parameters.
After epoch transition, the new seed must be computed via iterative keccak256 based on epoch number, and the cache must be regenerated using keccak512 chain with 3 rounds of RandMemoHash.
Cache and dataset sizes must be determined by finding the highest prime below the linear growth target (initial 2^24 for cache, 2^30 for dataset, plus per-epoch growth).
Light client verification must produce identical results to full verification by generating dataset items on-the-fly from cache using 256 parent accesses per item.
Ethash memory hardness must make ASIC-based mining impractical, preventing centralization of mining power.
Nodes must have sufficient memory to store the epoch cache; failure to do so forces reliance on full nodes for block verification.
The keccak256 and keccak512 hash functions used in Ethash must be cryptographically secure; PoW security depends on hash function integrity.
The FNV hash function used in the hashimoto mix must use standard FNV-1a parameters (prime 0x01000193) and produce deterministic, non-associative results.
After the light client hashimoto loop generates and returns a dataset item, the verification must continue to the next iteration until all 64 iterations complete.
